channel.title: Insurance Daily
channel.description: A ten-minute briefing on the US insurance market, every weekday morning. Rates and capacity, carrier appetite, claims and catastrophe losses, regulation, M&A and the insurtech deals that matter. Written for agents and brokers who need to know what moved before their first call of the day.

item.title: 24 September 2026 — Insurance Daily
item.description:
Thursday 24 September 2026. Today's US insurance briefing for agents and brokers.
- Here’s where thousands of homeowners face higher insurance bills after FEMA updated its flood maps (MarketWatch) - MultiPlan antitrust ruling raises questions for self-funded plans (Insurance Business America) - State of Emergency Declared in California in Anticipation of More El Niño-driven Storms (Carrier Management) - US Northeast Braces for Flooding as Coastal Storm Brews (Claims Journal) - Despite State Law, Only 8 of 160 Texas Utilities Filed Wildfire Response Plans (Carrier Management) - Benefits data moves to center of broker renewal talks (Insurance Business America) - Brown & Brown courts CFOs with 2027 health costs climbing (Insurance Business America) - Cyber Threats the Top Business Concern as AI Heightens Risk: Travelers Risk Index (Carrier Management)
Also: Insurance moves: Brown & Brown, Brown & Riding and Lockton; Cargo Theft a Top Concern for Majority of Retail Loss Control Leaders; Brokers keep agent-of-record status in eHealth CHOICE enrollment deal
